profile: NEW:Lewis Capaldi (Someone You Loved, with TMS)

add_characteristics.text: Melody first: brings a parked verse and pre-chorus melody to the room, and the lyric is finished fast and collaboratively there. Accounts of the details conflict.
Deliberately widened scope: from one breakup to loss in general, so the song fits a breakup and bereavements. His own later accounts of the subject vary.
Plain, image-light, wholly sincere lyric carried by melody and a raw vocal; critics call it generic by design.
The humour stays outside the songs, in the public persona; he says humour is what lets him own his flaws.
Sparse arrangement with TMS: piano and voice, drums rejected, strings only in the middle eight.

coverage: Rests on one song, 'Someone You Loved' (single 2018-11-08), and interviews from 2019-2020. Round-1 sources on 'Survive' (ST-S12 to ST-S16) were not re-read. Does not cover 'Before You Go', 'Hold Me While You Wait' (written with Jamie Hartman and Jamie N Commons, SB-S3#Q6) or his other co-writers. A reference summary, never an instruction to imitate.

profile: NEW:Adele (Someone Like You, with Dan Wilson)

add_characteristics.text: Arrives with the story and the opening verse lines; the co-writer's role is music, simplicity and protecting the plain words.
Deliberately personal frame: a real situation (a married ex, an uninvited visit), not generalised.
The irony is carried by one qualifier in the title and chorus, which are sung straight.
Demo as record: the first sincere take, piano and voice, kept over an orchestral version.

coverage: One song (2011) from 21. Adele's own words reach it only through Wikipedia and Songfacts relays. Does not cover her work with Paul Epworth or Greg Kurstin, or later albums. A reference summary, never an instruction to imitate.

add_characteristics.text: Honest, direct phrasing over clever wording, on chords with enough space to speak over.
Refused a bridge the label asked for, because the song had said what it needed and the space was for the crowd.
A choir built from layered takes of one voice in different registers; strings only near the end.
Changed a gendered word years later so the song could still be sung truthfully.

coverage: One song (2014), from one Song Exploder transcript. Does not cover the later catalogue or the Petty/Lynne credit dispute beyond its outcome. A reference summary, never an instruction to imitate.

add_characteristics.text: Grief written up-tempo on purpose, to celebrate the person and the move toward acceptance.
A stubborn chorus: the first one wasn't good enough for the subject, so the song waited months.
Observed strangers and a found phrase (a grave inscription) widen a private loss without explaining it.
Regional and social detail (North Shields, guilt over the cost-of-living crisis) sits beside the personal story; works from phone demos and believes in catching a song while it is hot.

coverage: One song (title track, single 2024-11-15), from one Song Exploder transcript. Does not cover 'Seventeen Going Under' or the earlier albums. A reference summary, never an instruction to imitate.
